In London, the Metropolitan Police confirmed on Saturday that it had received correspondence in 2019 detailing a "number of claims" regarding Mr Markle. The force shared the information with the Duke and Duchess of Sussex at the time but did not refer the matters to other international policing agencies. The Met is now conducting an internal review of how the information was handled.

In a recent statement, the Duchess addressed the historic correspondence, saying it contained "disturbing allegations" regarding her father.

"I am deeply distressed," Meghan said. "My thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."

She noted that the revelations explained why she had taken steps to distance herself from her father and prevent him from meeting her children.

title: Fin whale filmed engulfing thousands of gallons off Welsh coast
summary: Remarkable drone footage has captured the world's second-largest animal lunging for food off the coast of Pembrokeshire. Experts have described the close-to-shore sighting of the elusive marine giant as a rare encounter.
content:
Extraordinary footage has captured the moment the planet's second-largest living creature lunged open-mouthed to engulf thousands of gallons of water off the coast of Wales.

The fin whale was filmed using a drone by videographer Rhys Morgan off Pembrokeshire, revealing the mammal's throat pleats expanding to take in vast volumes of water and krill.

Mr Morgan said it was "complete luck" that he managed to film the giant feeding alongside dolphins while on a fishing trip with a friend.

Second only in size to the blue whale, the fin whale can grow up to 24 metres (79ft) in length and weigh as much as 70 tonnes. Despite their immense proportions, the fast-swimming creatures are notoriously elusive, spending most of their lives in the open ocean and often surfacing only briefly before disappearing beneath the waves.

Mr Morgan, who works at an oil refinery and pursues wildlife videography in his spare time, said he was raised on the water but was still left awestruck by the encounter.

"It's pretty incredible really," he said. "It makes you feel very small out there. We do what we can to keep our distance in the boat, but unfortunately nature can have a mind of its own sometimes. There's been times when we've been anchored up fishing with nothing happening, and a whale has popped up next to us."

Dr Marianna Chimienti, a lecturer in marine top predator ecology at Bangor University, described the sighting as a "rare and fortunate encounter".

"It is normal that the fin whale comes and feeds at the surface, as it is part of the species' foraging strategy, but being in coastal water is quite spectacular," she explained. "In theory, they should have migrated."

Fin whales consume a diet primarily consisting of krill, small schooling fish and squid. Due to the modest size of their prey, adult whales must eat continuously to sustain themselves, consuming up to 2,000kg of food each day.

title: Hundreds displaced as Israeli forces demolish homes in Hebron
summary: Hundreds of Palestinian families have been displaced in Hebron following extensive demolitions by Israeli forces in the occupied West Bank. The operation follows a checkpoint attack that left two Israeli soldiers dead just days before Israel's general election.
content:
The Israeli military has launched an extensive operation in the occupied West Bank, demolishing homes and commercial properties in the city of Hebron and displacing hundreds of Palestinian residents, according to local officials.

Footage verified from the city shows substantial devastation caused by military bulldozers, with at least one entire street reduced to rubble. Israeli security forces have also established a tight cordon around Hebron, severely curtailing movement for its roughly 200,000 inhabitants.

The military operation was announced by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu following the deaths of two Israeli soldiers, who were killed by two Palestinian gunmen during an attack at a checkpoint on Friday. Three other soldiers were wounded, while both assailants were shot dead at the scene.

Mr Netanyahu declared that structures in the vicinity of the attack and the neighbourhoods from which the gunmen originated would be systematically destroyed.

Hebron Mayor Youssef al-Jaabari said more than 1,000 residents had already been displaced by the operation, which has focused heavily on the Ein Deir Baha and Farsh al-Hawa districts. He said homes, businesses, industrial facilities and basic infrastructure had been flattened, with dozens of families forced to spend the night without shelter after their properties were marked for destruction.

Local authorities estimate that up to 2,500 people could ultimately be displaced across an urban area spanning roughly 0.35 sq km. Regional governors confirmed that more than 200 families had lost their homes in the opening phase of the demolitions.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) stated that it was targeting dozens of sites across the West Bank in operations expected to continue over several days.

Israel has long maintained a policy of demolishing homes belonging to Palestinians accused of carrying out attacks against Israelis. Human rights organisations have repeatedly condemned the measure as a form of collective punishment prohibited under international humanitarian law.

The escalation comes during an intense political moment in Israel, with a general election scheduled to take place in four days. Mr Netanyahu, campaigning heavily on a national security platform, suspended formal campaign events to visit Hebron in tactical body armour.

Addressing reporters, the prime minister warned that forces would move "house to house" to eliminate insurgent infrastructure, adding that plans had been reviewed for the widest military campaign in the West Bank since 1967.

The Palestinian Authority has appealed for urgent international intervention to halt forced displacement. Local leaders in Hebron have characterised the military action as politically motivated, alleging it is aimed at consolidating far-right voter support in the run-up to the poll.

title: Don't fall for this - how to protect yourself from AI scams
summary: Shoppers and internet users are being warned to exercise heightened caution as criminals deploy artificial intelligence to supercharge online fraud. From cloned retail storefronts to deepfake voice calls, trading standards officers have issued a new watchlist to help consumers spot synthetic scams.
key_takeaways: Fraudsters are using generative AI to build convincing fake UK retail websites, clone voices of family members, and automate personalised phishing.
Consumer group Which? warns that traditional red flags like typos or poor grammar can no longer be relied upon to identify scam messages.
Authorities advise verifying company registrations independently and never sending money or sensitive data under urgent pressure.
content:
Shoppers are being urged to exercise heightened vigilance over where they buy online, as criminal syndicates increasingly deploy artificial intelligence to supercharge financial scams.

Fraudsters have created sophisticated websites posing as family-owned British retailers offering high-quality domestic products, often illustrated with synthetic images of traditional UK high streets.

When consumers place orders, however, the goods either never materialise or turn out to be cheap, mass-produced items shipped from overseas, trading standards officers warn.

AI-generated imagery, alongside voice cloning and deepfake video technology, is increasingly being weaponised to deceive the public out of their savings, according to National Trading Standards. For the first time, the body has compiled a dedicated AI scam watchlist highlighting the primary tools and tactics criminals are deploying.

Key threats identified include cloned retail websites launched in minutes at minimal cost, long-term romance scams where AI chatbots remember personal details over months, and voice-cloned audio used to impersonate relatives requesting emergency funds.

Error-free, highly personalised phishing emails, text messages, and social media adverts are also being generated at unprecedented scale. Consumer group Which? cautioned that traditional scam-spotting techniques, such as looking for spelling mistakes or grammatical errors, are no longer reliable indicators.

To stay protected, trading standards officers recommend never transferring money, gift cards, or financial details to anyone you have not met in person, researching company addresses independently, and checking the Financial Conduct Authority register before acting on financial advice.

Above all, experts advise pausing before making any payment or sharing personal data, noting that criminals rely heavily on manufactured urgency to force victims into acting before they have time to verify the claim.
why_it_matters: The democratisation of generative AI has lowered the technical barrier for cybercrime, rendering traditional consumer awareness training obsolete and forcing regulators and banks to rethink digital identity verification.

title: Sam Fender calls out ticket prices ahead of stadium tour
summary: Musician Sam Fender has intervened to lower ticket prices ahead of his 2027 stadium tour after criticising inflated costs shared online. The singer also confirmed that general standing areas would not be split into premium front and back tiers.
key_takeaways: Sam Fender promised to reduce ticket prices for his summer 2027 stadium tour across Newcastle, London, Cardiff, Edinburgh, Dublin, and Manchester.
The singer rejected plans to divide standing areas into separate price tiers, questioning how the practice became normalised in live music.
His intervention follows growing backlash across the music industry over dynamic pricing and soaring concert costs.
content:
Sam Fender has spoken out against the cost of concert tickets ahead of his upcoming stadium tour, pledging to lower prices before they go on sale.

The 32-year-old musician announced his Proper Massive Stadium Tour earlier this week, with dates scheduled across Newcastle, Cardiff, London, Edinburgh, Dublin, and Manchester in summer 2027.

Although tickets have yet to be released, Fender responded directly to social media reports outlining the expected pricing tiers, stating he was unhappy with the figures.

"They're getting changed," he wrote on Instagram. "It got inflated well more than I'd had in mind. It should only be inflated in relation to the cost of putting the show on."

The North Shields singer also confirmed that general admission standing would not be divided into separate front and rear pricing zones, a practice that has become increasingly common at major arena and stadium events.

"The standing will not be split as well, I had no idea about it," Fender added. "I have no idea how this was normalised in gigs... it won't be happening on this tour."

Tickets are scheduled to go on general sale on Friday morning following a midweek pre-sale. Fender joins a growing number of recording artists raising concerns over the affordability of live music for fans amid rising production and ticketing fees.
why_it_matters: As live concert prices face mounting scrutiny from fans and consumer watchdogs, high-profile artists actively intervening against tiered standing and price inflation could pressure promoters to reform stadium ticketing practices.

title: How the UK state pension compares with other wealthy countries
summary: As debate intensifies over the future of the triple lock formula, international comparisons reveal how UK retirement benefits stack up against other developed nations. While automatic workplace enrolment narrows the gap, those relying solely on the state pension face stark disparities.
key_takeaways: Combined with mandatory workplace schemes, UK retirement benefits average 54.2% of pre-retirement earnings, below the OECD average of 63.2%.
The state pension budget is set to exceed £150bn annually, prompting plans to reform the triple lock link to average earnings from 2030.
The UK faces a significant gender pension gap, with women receiving roughly a third less than men due to career breaks and reliance on private pots.
content:
How nations fund retirement — and how much pensioners receive — remains one of the most fiercely debated fiscal questions across developed economies.

In the United Kingdom, the triple lock formula, which increases the state pension by whichever is highest out of 2.5%, average earnings growth, or inflation, has allowed retirement benefits to rise faster than workers' wages since 2011. Yet rising housing and living costs mean pensioner poverty has still edged upwards over the past decade.

With the annual cost of the state pension set to surpass £150bn, the government plans to introduce a revised system in 2030 that maintains increases in line with inflation or 2.5%, while removing the automatic annual link to average wage growth.

International comparisons compiled by the OECD highlight the trade-offs of the British model. Measured by the replacement rate — how generous a typical pension is relative to average working earnings — the basic UK state pension appears modest compared with European neighbours.

When mandatory workplace pension auto-enrolment is included, UK retirement income after tax reaches 54.2% of average earnings, compared with an OECD average of 63.2% across wealthy nations. Voluntary private and occupational pensions narrow that gap further, but leave individuals who rely solely on the state payout significantly worse off than counterparts abroad.

However, the heavy reliance on private workplace pots has exacerbated the gender pension gap. While men in wealthy nations typically receive 22.8% more in retirement income than women, in the UK women receive roughly a third less on average, reflecting lower lifetime pay, part-time work, and career breaks.

With ageing populations projected to drive pension spending sharply higher by 2060 across most developed countries, economists note that balancing fiscal sustainability with adequate protection for the poorest retirees remains a defining challenge for policymakers.
why_it_matters: As demographic shifts strain public finances across Western economies, the UK's transition away from the full triple lock toward private auto-enrolment serves as a crucial test case for managing sovereign debt while preventing old-age poverty.

title: Between quick wins and big dreams lies Burnham's biggest test
summary: As Chancellor John Healey prepares to deliver the government's Budget, the administration faces a pivotal transition from popular micro-policies to tough fiscal choices. With borrowing and public spending under pressure, maintaining party unity will be tested.
key_takeaways: The upcoming Budget marks the end of the government's initial 'politics of trying' phase, setting out long-term tax and spending priorities.
Ministers face tight fiscal constraints, with £1 in every £13 of government expenditure currently consumed by debt interest.
Expected measures include targeted levies on banks, regulatory reform for small businesses, devolution powers, and household energy support.
content:
Giving the north of England a chance to host the world's biggest sporting event with a £7m feasibility fund for a 2040 'Northern Games' captures the government's initial strategy: combining eye-catching long-term ambitions with targeted, everyday interventions.

Ministers have prided themselves on what insiders call 'the politics of trying' — focusing on tangible measures such as curbing unfair parking charges and anti-social behaviour on public transport while signalling broader national renewal.

Yet this week's Budget marks a decisive shift. Senior officials describe the upcoming statement by Chancellor John Healey as the first major fiscal test of the administration, laying the groundwork for a 10-year national plan and a demanding spending review.

Bound by manifesto commitments not to raise headline rates of income tax, VAT, or National Insurance for workers, the Treasury has limited room for manoeuvre. Public borrowing, taxation, and debt servicing remain at historic highs, with £1 in every £13 of state spending currently directed toward paying interest on existing debt.

Rather than dramatic giveaways, Westminster expectations point toward a measured package featuring targeted taxes on the banking sector, deregulation for small enterprises, expanded devolution for regional leaders, and measures to address rising winter energy bills.

Maintaining the unusually harmonious mood among backbench MPs will be critical. While increased ministerial accessibility has bolstered internal morale, upcoming decisions on welfare reform, defence funding, and economic growth will test the fragile equilibrium between the party's left and right wings.
why_it_matters: The Budget will define whether the government can stimulate economic growth and protect public services without spooking bond markets or breaking its core tax pledges.

title: Plan for Northern Olympics to get £7m in Healey's Budget
summary: Chancellor John Healey will allocate £7m in Wednesday's Budget for a full feasibility study into hosting the Olympic Games across northern England in the 2040s. The proposal is backed by regional mayors, UK Sport, and the British Olympic Association.
key_takeaways: A £7m fund will finance a comprehensive feasibility study into a potential 'Northern Games' bid for the 2040s.
The assessment will evaluate venue sharing across northern cities, transport infrastructure requirements, and overall taxpayer costs.
While sporting bodies welcomed the move, opposition critics urged careful scrutiny of costs amid ongoing economic pressures.
content:
A £7m fund to explore bringing the Olympic and Paralympic Games to northern England is set to be announced in Chancellor John Healey's Budget on Wednesday.

The Treasury will allocate the funding for a comprehensive feasibility study examining a potential bid for a 'Northern Games' to be staged in the 2040s.

The United Kingdom last hosted the Olympics in London in 2012, an event that cost an estimated £8.9bn and generated billions in reported economic activity and regeneration.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the initiative aimed to bring the excitement and economic opportunity of the Games directly to towns and cities across the North, uniting the country behind a shared national project.

Following an initial assessment by UK Sport earlier this year—spearheaded by northern mayors and celebrated Olympians including Dame Laura Kenny and Dame Sarah Storey—the full study will examine transport links, venue requirements, community legacy, and financial viability.

The British Olympic Association, ParalympicsGB, and UK Sport welcomed the commitment in a joint statement. Meanwhile, Conservative shadow sports minister Louie French said that while hosting the Games could provide a positive boost, the financial costs required careful scrutiny.
why_it_matters: A multi-city Northern Olympic bid represents a major test of the UK's regional devolution agenda, potentially channelling billions in long-term transport and regeneration investment outside London.

title: Ukraine's Starlink connection restored after speed limits lifted
summary: Ukraine's defence ministry has confirmed that satellite internet provider Starlink has returned to stable operation following days of restricted connectivity. The disruptions had hobbled military drone missions amid escalating diplomatic friction over strikes on Russian infrastructure.
content:
Ukraine now has a stable connection to Starlink after days of restricted connectivity across the satellite internet network, the country's defence minister has confirmed.

Ukrainian forces rely extensively on Starlink and its military-grade counterpart, Starshield, to pilot unmanned aerial vehicles and coordinate operations along the frontline. Kyiv had previously claimed that US President Donald Trump instructed owner Elon Musk to impose limitations on the system, an assertion Mr Trump denied before later stating that Musk had "put it back".

Under the recent restrictions, Ukrainian drones reportedly lost connection whenever they reached speeds of 161km/h (100mph) or higher. Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara announced on Saturday that speeds exceeding 400km/h were now achievable once more, indicating full operational capacity had returned.

"This result is above all important for our front, for our soldiers, for the operation of drones, for logistics and for communications," Mr Khmara said in an official statement.

The satellite network, comprising thousands of low Earth orbit spacecraft operated by SpaceX, has formed a digital backbone for Ukrainian forces, particularly in remote combat zones. While commercial Starlink terminals are widely deployed, Ukraine also uses Starshield, a secure government variant that Musk previously suggested was under Pentagon oversight.

The service limitations arose during a period of sharp diplomatic disagreement between Washington and Kyiv over Ukrainian deep-strike operations targeting Russian energy facilities. Mr Trump has criticised the strikes on Russian oil refineries, arguing they risk driving up global fuel prices, while Kyiv insists the targets are vital to cutting off the Kremlin's primary source of war funding.

President Volodymyr Zelensky also suggested the US had threatened to curtail intelligence sharing unless the cross-border strikes were halted, another claim the White House has rejected.

Meanwhile, intense fighting has continued across the front. Russia's defence ministry claimed its air defence units brought down more than 600 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones overnight, with attacks reported in several regions and occupied Crimea, where local authorities reported power cuts. In turn, Ukrainian officials stated their forces successfully struck a missile component facility, a chemical plant, and an aircraft at a military base inside Russian territory.

title: Met Police did not share letter detailing claims against Meghan's father, force confirms
summary: Scotland Yard has confirmed it received a letter in 2019 containing allegations about the Duchess of Sussex's estranged father, Thomas Markle, but did not pass it to other law enforcement agencies. The Metropolitan Police is currently reviewing its handling of the correspondence and deciding whether to refer itself to the police watchdog.
content:
A letter containing a "number of claims" relating to the Duchess of Sussex's father was received by the Metropolitan Police in 2019, Scotland Yard has confirmed.

The force stated that the details, which concerned alleged offences outside the UK, were forwarded to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex for security reasons, but were not shared with any other law enforcement bodies.

The Met is now reviewing its handling of the matter and considering whether to refer itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC).

Reports emerged on Friday alleging that child sexual abuse images had been discovered at the former Philippines home of Meghan's estranged father, Thomas Markle. The 82-year-old, who currently resides in the United States, has strongly denied possessing any such material.

On Friday, the Duchess released a statement saying she had been alerted to "disturbing allegations" regarding her father in 2018. Following the Met's clarification that the letter was received in January 2019, a spokesperson for Meghan said "any discrepancy of a few months" was an understandable consequence of time passing.

In an official statement, Scotland Yard said: "Following a thorough review of Met Police systems and records, we have confirmed that in January 2019, we received a letter containing a number of claims about alleged offending outside the United Kingdom.

"It was sent to the MPS Protection Command to raise concerns in relation to the security of the Duchess of Sussex. The letter was reviewed and a decision was made that it should be passed to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex for their awareness. The details of the allegations in the letter were not shared with other law enforcement agencies.

"The MPS is reviewing the handling of this matter in 2019 and considering whether a referral to the IOPC is necessary to review our approach."

Mr Markle relocated to the Philippines last year after suffering multiple strokes. He is understood to be receiving treatment at a rehabilitation facility in Florida.

The claims came to light after Meghan's half-brother, Thomas Markle Jnr, alleged he discovered illegal media at his father's former residence and contacted the US Federal Bureau of Investigation in July.

In her earlier statement, Meghan said that when she was informed of the claims, she received assurances that they were being investigated. She added that she hoped the public could understand why she maintained distance from her father and did not permit him contact with her children.

Authorities in the Philippines have confirmed that an anti-human trafficking and child sexual exploitation task force is currently investigating the allegations. Philippines Interior Minister Jonvic Remulla confirmed that national police had secured a computer from the residence for digital forensic analysis.

title: On the run: The £33m tax fraudster evading justice in Dubai
summary: Arif Patel, sentenced in his absence to 20 years in prison for masterminding a massive VAT carousel scam, continues to evade British justice. Despite a £90m confiscation order, the fugitive remains at large in the UAE while attempting to challenge rulings from overseas.
content:
One of the UK's most prolific fraudsters, branded by a judge as a "breathtakingly arrogant" and "totally dishonest" criminal, remains on the run in Dubai after siphoning more than £33m of public money.

Arif Patel, originally from Preston in Lancashire, was convicted following an extensive, years-long inquiry led by HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC). Investigators established that he had orchestrated an elaborate web of fraudulent transactions intended to fleece the taxpayer of up to £90m.

Patel fled Britain in 2011 after being granted bail to travel abroad and never returned. In 2023, he was convicted in his absence and handed a 20-year prison sentence. However, he has yet to serve a single day behind bars.

During the early 2000s, Patel cultivated the public image of a booming northern entrepreneur. His textile firm, Faisaltex, manufactured everyday garments including nightwear and socks for major high street retailers. In 2006, his personal fortune was estimated at £105m, earning him a place on the Sunday Times Rich List. He invested heavily in commercial property, bought into Preston North End Football Club through his teenage son, and unveiled plans for a £100m, 19-storey city centre skyscraper.

Behind this lavish exterior, however, lay a sophisticated carousel fraud. The criminal enterprise relied on circular chains of counterfeit trade, repeatedly exporting and re-importing consignments of goods across international borders to generate fraudulent VAT repayment claims from the tax authorities.

While most carousel syndicates focused on high-value electronics such as mobile handsets or microprocessors, Patel's operation exploited the textile trade, creating an operation that proved far harder to detect. By the time authorities unpicked the network, tens of millions had already been diverted into overseas accounts.

In 2011, Patel appeared at Bolton Crown Court on charges including conspiracy to cheat the public revenue, money laundering, and selling counterfeit goods. After successfully applying to travel to Dubai on bail, he vanished, joining two of his brothers who had already absconded. Across subsequent trials, 24 members of the wider syndicate were convicted, receiving custodial terms totalling more than 116 years.

Attempts to extradite Patel from the United Arab Emirates have so far been unsuccessful. Former investigators have disclosed that intermediaries acting on Patel's behalf later sought to negotiate financial settlements to avoid prison time, claiming the fugitive was prepared to repay stolen funds but refused to submit to a custodial sentence.

Authorities subsequently imposed a £90.5m confiscation order on Patel to recover proceeds of his criminal activity. Yet more than a year later, no money has been recovered, as Patel has continued to lodge legal challenges from abroad through the Court of Appeal.

In recent years, an array of online profiles, promotional articles, and social media videos have emerged portraying an individual named Arif Patel in Dubai as a prominent investor and philanthropist. Despite the continued attempts at digital reputation management, Patel remains an officially designated fugitive wanted by British law enforcement.

title: Vincent Kompany: Bayern Munich manager's recovery will take 'weeks' following collapse
summary: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany will need weeks to recover after collapsing at the club's training ground on Friday. The former Manchester City captain remains in a stable condition in hospital as medical evaluations continue.
content:
Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany will require weeks to recover after collapsing at the club's training ground on Friday, sporting director Max Eberl has confirmed.

The 40-year-old former Manchester City and Belgium captain remains in hospital in a stable condition, where medical personnel are continuing to carry out tests.

Eberl stated that while the German giants had explored the possibility of postponing Sunday's Bundesliga fixture against Freiburg, they concluded that playing the match remained the best course of action.

"Vinnie will be given all the time he needs. We are not starting to put together any timeframes," Eberl said. "We need to firstly figure out what it is and then we'll discuss calmly what the recovery time is to be. We won't be talking about days, but weeks. We need to all be clear on that."

Kompany was rushed to hospital after collapsing while observing Bayern's reserve side in training. The Belgian had reportedly been suffering from a viral illness earlier in the week, forcing him to miss Tuesday's pre-match media briefing prior to their Champions League tie against Arsenal.

Despite his illness, Kompany took charge from the technical area on Wednesday evening, prompting Eberl to reflect on whether the club ought to have intervened sooner.

"The fact is, we protect our coach wherever we can," Eberl explained. "If a coach says he feels ready to do something, then we're not going to say 'we won't allow that' if we don't know what's going on. It's also everyone's own responsibility to say, 'I can't carry on now'.

"Vinnie's a hard worker. If you don't listen to the subtle signals your body sends, eventually it will scream out in pain. Vinnie will be given that time, and we'll continue to try, even more than before, to protect him from himself."

Assistant coach Aaron Danks has visited Kompany in hospital and confirmed that football matters had been temporarily put to one side.

"I explained to him that we would be having no football conversations," Danks said. "It was just checking in on his health and making sure he's OK. All the football operations are in our hands and we'll work together as a team to keep the club moving forward."

Kompany enjoyed a decorated 11-year spell as a player at Manchester City, winning four Premier League titles, before stepping into management with Anderlecht and Burnley. He took the reins at the Allianz Arena in May 2024, steering Bayern to consecutive domestic league titles.

title: British mother dies trying to rescue sons in Bahamas
summary: A 36-year-old British woman has died after attempting to rescue her two sons when they were swept away while snorkelling in the Bahamas. Both children were subsequently brought to safety, local police said.
content:
A British woman has died after attempting to rescue her two young sons when they were swept away by strong currents while snorkelling in the Bahamas.

The Royal Bahamas Police Force said officers on the island of Bimini had launched an inquiry following the sudden death of the 36-year-old woman, believed to be from Stapleford in Nottinghamshire.

According to authorities, the woman was snorkelling with her husband and their two sons near the southern tip of the island on Tuesday morning when a strong current carried the children away.

In an attempt to reach her sons, the woman was also swept out to sea. Both children were subsequently pulled from the water safely.

In a statement, the Royal Bahamas Police Force said officers were alerted shortly after 10:00 local time that a woman was unresponsive at the North Bimini Ferry Dock.

She had been brought ashore by rescuers who administered CPR before emergency teams transported her to a local medical clinic, where she was pronounced dead.

Police said foul play is not suspected at this stage, and an autopsy will be carried out to establish the exact cause of death.

A spokesperson for the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office said: "Our thoughts are with the family of a British woman who has died in the Bahamas. We are in contact with the local authorities and providing support to her family."

title: Gianni Infantino insists he has backing of 'vast majority' of world football
summary: Fifa president Gianni Infantino has dismissed suggestions he should resign following controversy over commercial rights plans, claiming broad global support. Speaking from Azerbaijan, he struck a defiant tone despite recent backlash from European and continental governing bodies.
content:
Fifa president Gianni Infantino has insisted he retains the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football, laughing off questions regarding whether he had considered resigning following a fierce backlash over commercial proposals.

In a rare interview, Infantino struck a defiant tone regarding his position in the wake of the controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, arguing it was not always simple to bring differing viewpoints together under one umbrella.

"There is nothing bad in disagreeing," he said. "We see it every day in so many countries in the world. It is OK to disagree. It is OK to have different points of view, but then we need to be able to move on."

Only two months ago, Infantino faced significant pressure to step down from the organisation he has led since 2016. The heads of European football's governing body Uefa, the Asian Football Confederation, and Concacaf signed a joint letter accusing the Fifa president of breaching trust through deception.

Under the FFE plans, which Infantino withdrew within days of their unveiling, a proportion of the governing body's commercial rights would have been transferred to a private investment firm. Uefa subsequently set a deadline demanding Fifa release all key documentation related to the proposal, warning that fundamental questions remained unanswered.

Since the joint letter was sent, Infantino has engaged in a whistle-stop global tour, visiting Morocco, the Dominican Republic, Cape Verde, and Japan to consolidate support. His re-election for a fourth term next year now appears largely assured after securing public endorsements from both the Asian Football Confederation and African member associations.

Infantino recently offered an apology to the Fifa Council regarding the communication and consultation surrounding the scheme. During that meeting, some members suggested he was not fit to lead the organisation if full disclosure was withheld.

When asked about the handover of the requested documents, Infantino remained non-committal, saying Fifa had to respect a "legal process" and was working through the matter.

Speaking in Baku during the Under-15 World Cup, Infantino admitted the administration had done "some things which are maybe less good", but called for enhanced dialogue with European authorities to mend fractured relationships.

Pressed on whether he had considered stepping aside, Infantino laughed off the suggestion. "I was elected by 211 member associations from all over the world," he said. "If we are serious about democracy and believing that everyone has the same vote and the same voice, we need to respect the views of the vast, vast majority."

Candidates intending to challenge Infantino in the upcoming presidential election must register by 18 November, though no rival contenders have yet emerged, leaving him poised to run unopposed.

title: Cost of living: How to keep your home warm without soaring energy bills
summary: As temperatures drop and household energy bills face further increases, simple domestic adjustments can help households stay warm. Consumer experts and families share cost-effective methods to retain heat without relying entirely on central heating.
content:
As autumn sets in and colder weather sweeps across the UK, many households are seeking practical ways to keep warm without immediately turning up the thermostat. With energy costs continuing to strain household budgets, taking simple preventative steps now could lead to substantial savings over the coming winter.

Health specialists caution that vulnerable individuals and the elderly should never compromise their well-being by sitting in freezing conditions. However, consumer experts and families across the country have shared effective strategies to retain household heat while managing costs.

Keeping the body warm is often the first line of defence. The British Heart Foundation advises wearing multiple thin layers rather than a single thick garment, as trapped air acts as natural insulation. Thermal undergarments, thick woollen socks, and warm meals such as stews and soups can significantly help maintain core body temperature throughout the day.

Bedding is another area where minor adjustments yield noticeable benefits. Upgrading to a winter duvet with a tog rating of 10.5 or higher, or placing an extra blanket beneath the mattress, helps insulate against cold draughts from beneath the bed. Electric blankets also represent an economical option; consumer watchdog Which? estimates that running one at full heat typically costs between 2p and 8p per hour. Fire services remind users to unplug electric blankets before sleeping unless fitted with a modern thermostat control, and to replace units older than ten years.

Simple measures to manage airflow can dramatically reduce heat loss. Closing doors between rooms, hanging heavy curtains, and deploying draught excluders around external door frames all help keep warmth confined to occupied spaces. Everyday household items, such as rolled-up towels or tights filled with old socks, make effective makeshift draught stoppers.

Letting natural sunlight into rooms during clear days warms indoor spaces naturally, provided curtains are drawn as soon as dusk falls to trap the residual warmth. In kitchens, leaving the oven door ajar after cooking allows excess heat to circulate into the room, provided caution is exercised in households with young children or pets.

For those who must use central heating, efficiency remains paramount. Bleeding radiators ensures they function properly, while moving large furniture away from heating elements prevents heat from being obstructed. Affixing heat-reflective foil behind radiators on external walls can also stop an estimated 35% of heat from escaping through brickwork.

Adjusting combi boiler flow temperatures and using the frost-protection valve settings on individual radiators can also curb consumption. With industry analysts forecasting further spikes in baseline energy bills into the new year, combining these low-cost adjustments can help households endure the winter chill without facing unmanageable bills.

title: California ballot: Voters to decide on world's first wealth tax targeting billionaires
summary: California voters are preparing to cast their ballots on Proposition 40, a historic one-off 5% wealth levy aimed at the state's ultra-rich. The proposal has divided political leaders and sparked warnings of an exodus among some of the world's wealthiest residents.
content:
Few places on the planet boast as many ultra-wealthy residents as California, a US state famed for coastal mansions, tech conglomerates and high-profile celebrities. Now, its electorate is set to decide whether the super-rich should surrender billions of dollars to bolster the state's healthcare system.

Proposition 40 seeks to impose a one-off 5% wealth tax on the total net worth of every California resident holding more than $1bn (£750m). Across the state, an estimated 200 individuals fall into this elite bracket, including Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg, media mogul Oprah Winfrey, and filmmaker George Lucas.

The measure aims to generate approximately $100bn (£75bn) to shore up state healthcare services, which face significant deficits following federal budget cuts. Public policy experts note that if passed, it would represent the world's first targeted levy on such an extreme bracket of the wealth distribution.

California represents the fourth-largest economy globally—surpassing both the UK and India in economic output—yet it simultaneously grapples with acute wealth disparities and the largest homeless population in the United States. Proponents argue the levy simply asks those who have prospered most to pay their fair share.

However, the proposition has provoked fierce resistance and warnings of capital flight. High-profile figures including Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin, as well as venture capitalist Peter Thiel, have reportedly relocated their primary residencies out of California ahead of the tax's retroactive application date.

Even prominent Democratic figures have voiced concern. Outgoing California Governor Gavin Newsom opposes the ballot, cautioning that driving away high-earning residents could severely damage the state's ongoing income tax base.

Independent economic analysts have also pointed to international precedents. While wealth taxes were once commonplace in Western Europe, most nations have abandoned them due to high administrative costs and capital flight, leaving only a handful of countries, including Norway and Switzerland, retaining such frameworks.

Public opinion in California remains on a knife-edge. Recent polling indicates 45% of likely voters support the initiative, 42% oppose it, and 13% remain undecided. With the vote fast approaching, the outcome will serve as a bellwether for wealth taxation across the globe.

title: UK to invest £100m in 'world-first' AI biosecurity lab
summary: The UK government is to invest £100m to establish a national AI Biosecurity Lab designed to counter emerging biological and cyber threats. The initiative will be supported by leading tech firms, including OpenAI and Anthropic, which have pledged £200m in model access credits.
content:
The UK is to establish a national AI Biosecurity Lab aimed at bolstering defences against emerging biological risks and technological hazards.

As part of the Budget, the government will commit £100m towards creating the facility, which ministers have described as a "world first".

The funding forms part of a broader package intended to reinforce national security against evolving cyber, biological, and AI-enabled threats.

Setting out the strategy, the government stressed the importance of harnessing the technology while mitigating its dangers.

"AI will transform daily life: every firm, community, hospital, school, and every aspect of our economy can benefit," Defence Secretary John Healey said.

"I understand and share the concerns of working people, so I am setting out a distinctively British approach to AI. One that doesn't leave workers behind and defends our national interest, while ensuring the benefits of AI-enabled growth are felt right across the country."

AI Minister Kanishka Narayan described the laboratory as a "major new global institution" that would combine scientific expertise to safeguard the public.

"That means staying ahead of emerging threats, from cyber attacks to biological risks, while building more of the critical technology our security depends on," Mr Narayan said.

The venture will be supported by leading commercial developers, with OpenAI and Anthropic providing £200m worth of credits to allow researchers to access and stress-test their models.

The Chancellor will also commit a further £120m to the UK's AI Security Institute (AISI). Established in 2023, the body is responsible for evaluating the safety and potential risks posed by the most powerful frontier models.

A further £60m will be directed towards a "National Cyber Shield" employing agentic AI to detect digital attacks, alongside £70m for a National Exposure and Real-Time Vulnerability (NERV) Centre to protect critical national infrastructure.

The increased investment comes amid mounting international scrutiny over the potential misuse of artificial intelligence, particularly its capacity to uncover software exploits or lower technical barriers to creating dangerous pathogens.
